_meta.purpose: Deterministic UK grid-connection rules (ENA EREC G98/G99/G100). The Decarbonarma agent applies these to tell a user which application they need, whether it must happen BEFORE install, and how much generation their supply can take. These are rules of thumb for domestic advice — the DNO's own network study is always final.
_meta.disclaimer: Guidance only. The homeowner's DNO (SSEN, UKPN, NGED, SP Energy Networks, Electricity North West, NIE) makes the binding decision. Always tell users to confirm with their DNO / MCS installer before ordering equipment.

key_principle: Two different limits that people confuse: (1) INVERTER / generation capacity = the total size of inverter(s) you install; (2) EXPORT capacity = the most you're allowed to push to the grid. The DNO mainly cares about export. A G100 export limiter lets you install a big inverter while capping export low — that's how homes run 12kW+ of inverters on a single phase with, say, a 6kW export cap.

g98.process: 'Fit and inform'. You can install FIRST, then notify the DNO within 28 days of commissioning. No prior approval needed.
g98.applies_when: Total generation+storage inverter capacity is at or below the per-phase limit AND export is within it.

g99.trigger: Any time inverter/export exceeds the G98 threshold (>3.68kW single phase, >11.04kW three phase).
g99.process: APPLY AND GET APPROVAL BEFORE YOU CONNECT OR COMMISSION. This is the critical timing point — do it before ordering/installing, not after.
g99.dno_response_time: Up to 45 working days (fast-track bands can be quicker).
g99.single_phase_ceiling_note: The G99 'A1' application band covers total aggregate generation up to ~17kW on single phase. Above that the DNO will normally require a three-phase supply. Treat ~16-17kW as the practical single-phase ceiling.
g99.three_phase_ceiling_note: A1 band up to 50kW three phase.

g100.what: Export Limitation Scheme. A compliant device must cut export to within the agreed limit within 5 seconds of exceeding it.
g100.why: Lets you install more inverter capacity than your export limit for self-consumption/battery, while guaranteeing the grid never sees more than the cap. Makes bigger systems approvable on constrained networks.
g100.typical: Common single-phase export caps: 3.68kW, 5kW, 6kW. The cap is set in the G99 offer.

steps: 1. Sum ALL inverter capacity (existing PV + new PV + battery inverter). Batteries count.
2. If single phase and total <= 3.68kW AND export <= 3.68kW -> G98 (fit & inform, 28 days after).
3. If three phase and total <= 11.04kW AND export <= 11.04kW -> G98.
4. Otherwise -> G99: MUST be approved before connecting. Include a G100 export limiter if export needs capping below inverter size.
5. If single phase and total > ~17kW -> expect DNO to require a three-phase supply upgrade (big, costly job).
6. Any INCREASE to an already-approved system (bigger inverter, extra panels) needs a G99 VARIATION to the existing connection agreement — not fit-and-inform, even if export is unchanged.
7. Zero-export / no-export systems still need the correct G98/G99 notification based on inverter capacity.

timing_warnings: G99 approval must be in hand BEFORE commissioning. Installing first and applying later can mean the DNO orders disconnection or refuses retrospective approval.
Battery-only additions still count toward inverter capacity and can tip a G98 system into G99 territory.
A change of inverter (e.g. swapping a 3.6kW for a 5kW) is a capacity increase -> G99 variation required first.

worked_example_single_phase.note: Illustrative single-phase case the agent can use to explain the maths.
worked_example_single_phase.mechanism: G99 approved with a 6kW G100 export limit; no network reinforcement required.
worked_example_single_phase.headroom: Against the ~17kW single-phase ceiling, ~4kW of capacity headroom. Swapping the 4.6kW unit for a 5kW one stays under the ceiling but needs a G99 variation (a capacity increase must be approved first).
